records.found: Nothing dated 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-09 bears on the test: no new controlled result, registry posting or regulator decision for a drug of this class was found. Two older points for the author: the registry entry used as the stage record (NCT04857996, last updated 2024-05-16) lists safety and tolerability as the trial's main measures, with vision among the secondary ones, while the test asks for the pre-stated main measure; and a company-reported controlled phase 1 result of 2026-03-26 (Rubedo's RLS-1496) is not in the records.

findings.what: The registry entry for Unity's eye trial (NCT04857996, the stage record) is unchanged since 2024-05-16; status completed, results posted 2024-05-16. Its two listed main measures are systemic and ocular safety and tolerability, not vision. The records do not note this, and the test wording asks for improvement on the pre-stated main measure.

Older fact the records do not hold: Rubedo Life Sciences announced preliminary results of a randomised, double-blind, controlled phase 1 trial of its drug RLS-1496 in people with psoriasis, saying it met its main measure and that aged cells fell in the middle and high dose groups. Company-reported, not peer-reviewed; the main measure is not named in the report read (the trade-press report of 2026-03-27; the company release itself refused the fetch).

Just before the window: a filing by Pulmatrix carrying a release from Eos SENOLYTIX on an interim rat study of its drug PTC-2105, described as partly working by removing aged cells; no human data, first human studies aimed at 2027.

Registry update to a Mayo Clinic placebo-controlled fisetin trial in COVID-19 (NCT04476953): still active, not recruiting, 80 people, no results posted; main completion now estimated March 2027. A different condition, so it bears only loosely.

records.found: On 2026-11-06 Nature Aging published a paper (Wu and colleagues) reporting that a mineral supplement, vanadyl sulfate, given by mouth, acts as a drug that kills aged cells, eases signs of ageing and lengthens life in male mice. That adds to the animal rung, which the entry already holds; it is not a human result, so the test for the next stage is not met. A paper in Cell dated 2026-11-02 reports another compound lowering markers of aged cells and improving function in old mice, with no lifespan result.

findings.what: Nature Aging: 'Altered protein cysteine reactivity in senescent cells is a vulnerability for senolysis to ameliorate aging' (Wu and colleagues). The abstract says the supplement eases ageing and age-related disorders and 'extends lifespan in male mice'. Peer-reviewed, mice only. Abstract read at Europe PMC (PMID 42995257) and date confirmed at Crossref; the journal page asked for a sign-in, so the size of the lifespan gain and the age at which dosing began were not read.

Cell: 'Fatty acid desaturation controls cellular fate decisions between senescence and ferroptosis' (Kuehnemann and colleagues). The abstract says a fatty acid given by mouth lowered markers of aged cells in old mice and improved age-related function; no lifespan measure. Abstract read at Europe PMC (PMID 42971201); the journal page refused the fetch.

records.found: On 2026-11-05 the trial registry first posted a completed Steadman Philippon Research Institute trial (NCT07918261) in which 82 healthy people aged 55 and over were randomly given one of two fisetin schedules, with the change in aged cells in blood at 45 days as its main measure. The trial ran from 2023-05-24 to 2024-01-30 and was registered only now; no results are posted, there is no placebo group, and there is no peer-reviewed report, so the test is not touched. An older company-reported result (Rubedo, 2026-03-26) that claims fewer aged cells in treated people is not in the records.

findings.what: Registry entry NCT07918261, 'Evaluation of Fisetin to Reduce Systemic Senescence', first posted 2026-11-05 (first submitted 2026-10-21): status completed, 82 enrolled, two fisetin schedules compared with no placebo group, main measure the change from the start in aged blood cells at 45 days. No results posted.

unmatched.what: European Heart Journal Open published a double-blind randomised trial (61 people randomised, 43 finished) of a multi-ingredient supplement aimed at ageing mechanisms; against control, the trial's main measure of blood-vessel function improved over six months, and artery stiffness and systolic blood pressure fell. Registry number NCT06145087. Abstract read at Europe PMC (PMID 42979377); the full paper and its funding statement were not read.
unmatched.why_it_matters: A small controlled trial in healthy adults reporting a positive main measure for a product sold against vascular ageing; it fits none of the aged-cell records, and the drop-out rate and funding would need checking before any use.
